entries.titleEn: Relaying Google Workspace MCP Approvals (input_required) to an Agent's Confirmation Dialog: A stdio Relay and the 60-Second Timeout Pitfall
entries.contentSnippet: Google Workspace MCP の承認（input_required）を agent の確認ダイアログに中継する ― stdio リレーと 60 秒タイムアウトの落とし穴 2026 年 11 月 24 日、Google Workspace のリモート MCP サーバーが GA になりました。Gmail / Drive / Docs / Sheets / Calendar などが、製品ごとに https://<product>mcp.googleapis.com/mcp/v1 で提供されています。2027 年 2 月 1 日以降、AI エージェントは REST API を直接呼ぶのではなく、この MCP サーバーか Workspace CLI を経由することが求められます。 ここで引っかかるのが 承認 です。Google 側は一部のツール呼び出しをいきなり実行せず、結果として input_required を返して「ユーザーに確認を取ってから再送して」と求めてきます。これは MCP 2026-07-28 のステートレスな形式（Multi Round-Trip Requests）で、従来の「サーバーからクライアントへ elicitation/create を送る」方式とは別物です。 手元の agent は、従来の elicitation/create （確認ダイアログ）には対応していても、この input_required 形式をまだ扱えないことがあります。そこでこの記事では、 Google の MCP サーバーと agent の間に ローカルの stdio リレー を挟み、上流の input_required を下流の elicitation/create に変換して中継する方法 を紹介します。検証は Claude Code（2.1.332）、 @modelcontextprotocol/sdk 1.32.2 で行いました。 この記事のコードは検証用（spike）です。本番利用を想定したエラー処理やトークン管理はしていません。

entries.title: How to choose the next safe step in application modernization
entries.titleJa: アプリケーションモダナイゼーションで次の安全な一歩を選ぶ方法
entries.titleEn: How to choose the next safe step in application modernization
entries.summaryJa: GitHub Copilotを使い、小規模なNode.jsゲームから大規模なJava製ERPまで公開アプリ4つで、既存の動作を確かめる証拠優先の手法を検証した。フレームワーク選定より先に回帰テストの土台を作る手順を示し、自社アプリにも応用できる。
entries.summaryEn: Using GitHub Copilot, the author tested an evidence-first approach on four public apps, from a small Node.js game to a large Java ERP system, gathering regression evidence before picking a framework. Teams can repeat it on their own application.
entries.contentSnippet: A request to modernize an application often starts with a technology question: Which framework should replace the old one? Before you choose, find out what still works. Then collect evidence that can act as a regression net for that behavior and show where modernization is necessary. I used an evidence-first method on four public applications, from a small Node.js game to a large Java enterprise resource planning (ERP) application. Each needed a different treatment, but the way I collected evidence, chose the next experiment, and decided on possible proof points was repeatable. This post walks through that process so you can apply it to one application of your own. It also shows how to encode the procedure in a GitHub Copilot agent skill while keeping architectural judgment with the people responsible for the system. The label on an application rarely tells you enough.

entries.title: More predictable notifications on GitHub.com
entries.titleJa: GitHub.comの通知がより予測しやすく変わります
entries.contentSnippet: Starting December 1, 2026, we’re migrating notifications on GitHub.com over the course of a week to make subscriptions more predictable, correct unexpected behavior, and support the growing scale of activity. During the rollout, notifications may behave differently for different users. No action is required, but the changes below may affect how you manage and filter notifications. This does not apply to GitHub Enterprise Server. Routine activity won’t resubscribe you: Previously, after manually unsubscribing, notification activities such as commenting, submitting a pull request review, changing a thread’s state, or merge queue activity resulted in a re-subscription. Now, those actions leave you unsubscribed. Being mentioned, assigned, or receiving a pull request review request will continue to resubscribe you since those actions ask for your attention.

entries.contentSnippet: From Files to Cited Answers in One API Call: Managed Ingestion and SearchDocuments in Agent Retrieval A guide to the new managed ingestion and SearchDocuments features in Agent Retrieval , for searching PDFs, Office files, and videos without writing an ingestion pipeline. Before an agent can answer a question about your PDFs, someone has to build the pipeline: parse every file, split it into chunks, embed each chunk, write the chunks to a vector database, and then learn that database's schema to query it. For video it gets harder: transcode the files, cut them into clips, embed the frames, and keep track of which second of which video each clip came from. Before: every step of the pipeline is custom code you write and maintain, separately for documents and for videos. Most of that code has nothing to do with your application.
entries.feedSnippet: Agent Retrieval in Vertex AI introduces managed ingestion and SearchDocuments to replace custom chunking and embedding pipelines. Developers can now import document and video files directly from Cloud Storage and query them with a single API call for cited page numbers and timestamped results. The feature supports hybrid retrieval, metadata filtering, reranking, and multimodal video audio search.

entries.contentSnippet: The GitHub Code Quality upload-code-coverage action now checks that your coverage report is in Cobertura XML format. If it isn’t in a supported format, the upload step fails and the Actions log shows this error: This file is not a Cobertura XML report. Upload a Cobertura XML report. Previously, these uploads appeared to succeed, but no coverage showed up on your pull requests. Now you’ll find out about the problem in the workflow run, with a clear next step. We’ve also made processing more forgiving for valid Cobertura reports. We no longer reject a report because of minor structural issues, and we skip individual lines that don’t have a usable line number or hit count instead of discarding the whole report.

entries.summaryJa: Microsoft Foundryのホステッドエージェントを自社VNetへ移す際、デプロイは成功してもAgentsページがタイムアウトする問題に対し、原因を切り分ける5つの確認項目とコマンドを紹介する。閉域構成を運用するチームに役立つ。
entries.summaryEn: Microsoft Foundry hosted agents moved into a private VNet can deploy fine yet leave the Agents page timing out. Five checks with commands help network teams in locked-down setups find the missing piece.
entries.contentSnippet: Over the last few weeks I have worked with several teams moving hosted agents into their own virtual network. Different industries, same five questions. This post answers each one with the commands I use to check it. Picture a financial services team running claims agents in a locked-down network. Public access on the Foundry resource is off. The agent subnet sits in a spoke VNet. Azure Cosmos DB, Storage and Azure AI Search sit behind private endpoints, some of them in a hub VNet. All outbound traffic goes through a firewall that inspects TLS. The deployment succeeds. Then the Agents page spins and fails with a timeout. Nothing is wrong with the agent. The network around it is missing one piece. Here is how to find it.

The agent can read the file and send email, so it fulfills the user request. Semantic governance policies, available in Preview in Gemini platform, enable enterprises to govern their agents and provide guardrails to stop that call before it runs. They check each tool call an agent proposes against what the user asked for and against rules you write in plain language. Permissions alone can't catch this. They say what an agent can do, not whether a particular call follows your rules.

entries.contentSnippet: Over the last few months I’ve worked with a lot of teams taking a hosted agent from pilot to production. A working demo is only the start. The questions that decide whether it ships come next: Will the subnet hold up when usage takes off? Can the agent call internal services that use our own certificates? Where exactly can it connect, and who decides? Can it run on the Azure Kubernetes Service (AKS) clusters we already operate? And what happens when a two-hour job gets interrupted? At Microsoft Ignite 2026, we’re announcing a solution to each of these challenges for hosted agents in Foundry Agent Service. Below you’ll find what’s new, what you can use today, and what’s still to come. The egress and private CA updates apply to managed hosted agents, the ones Foundry runs for you; BYO-AKS support will be documented separately.

entries.titleEn: TokenEconomizer: Learning from Experience to Make AI Coding Agents More Efficient
entries.contentSnippet: Developers use AI coding agents in the same codebases day after day, yet agents often start each session from scratch: rediscovering familiar facts, loading unused tools, and repeating unsuccessful approaches. TokenEconomizer is an open-source plugin that learns from an agent’s past sessions in a repository to reduce waste in future sessions, without modifying the agent or its underlying model. Across 277 real bug-fixing tasks, TokenEconomizer reduced costs by 18.4–30.9% across multiple AI coding agents. Costs fell in every repository tested, while task success rates remained broadly stable. AI coding agents are increasingly helping developers fix bugs and build features largely on their own, but every interaction with their models consumes tokens. In each session , an agent sends instructions, tool descriptions, and session history to its model.
entries.feedSnippet: AI coding agents can waste time and tokens relearning the same lessons. TokenEconomizer is an open-source plugin that builds on past sessions to cut costs while maintaining task success. It’s a path toward coding agents that learn not only how to solve tasks, but also how to spend computation more effectively. entries.contentSnippet: How Meta's Reality Labs brought Cuttlefish and its QEMU backend to macOS and Apple silicon. Meta’s Reality Labs builds products such as AI glasses . Emulators provide us with a way to scale development and testing without relying on scarce physical hardware. Testing software for non-phone Android devices depends on how closely a virtual device reproduces the software behavior of the physical product. While a lightweight emulator like Goldfish gets you part of the way, differences from the real device can hide bugs until later in development. Cuttlefish is the Android Open Source Project’s (AOSP’s) virtual-device framework for testing Android software against virtual hardware.

entries.summaryEn: GitHub Copilot's agent skills package repeatable task instructions in a versioned directory built around SKILL.md, shareable across agents, though the runtime must supply tools, credentials, and permissions. This helps developers turn personal know-how into team assets.
entries.contentSnippet: How many times this week did you re-explain the same task to an agent? How many times did you ask your colleague with deep institutional knowledge how to solve a specific problem? That context shouldn’t be lost in a chat or locked in one person’s head. Agent skills let you capture repeatable instructions so you and your agents can reuse them. The skill you write for yourself tonight can later become part of a team’s pipeline. An agent skill is a versioned directory centered on a SKILL.md file that describes when and how to do a repeatable task. You can share those instructions across agents, but the environment still needs to provide the tools, credentials, and permissions to carry them out. A skill can describe how to query a database, for example, but it doesn’t grant access to that database.
entries.feedSnippet: Agent skills capture repeatable engineering work in files teams can review and reuse, while tools, project context, and permissions remain specific to the host that runs them. entries.summaryEn: A GitHub Copilot guide to agentic engineering, noting a week of over 1.2 billion commits and a 441% rise in review time, to help developers manage work beyond code generation.
entries.contentSnippet: This October, GitHub saw more than 1.2 billion commits in one week—over 400% more than a year earlier. This is more commits than GitHub received in all of 2025. Chances are, you’re generating more code than you were a year ago. But ask yourself: do you feel 400% more productive than you were last year? Building software takes more than a good prompt. As AI speeds up implementation, software developers are feeling more pressure in other places: a Faros AI study found that pull requests spent 441% longer in review when teams went from low to high AI adoption. As a software developer, you gather requirements and steer implementation, review changes and evaluate test results, then investigate what happens in production. Agents can help you work more efficiently across all of these stages: Plan, Build, Verify, and Observe.
entries.feedSnippet: Writing code got faster. The work around it didn't. entries.summaryJa: Cursorにエージェントと音声通話で対話できるボイスチャットが登場し、Grok Voiceで動作します。エージェントウィンドウ、IDE、ウェブ、iOSで使え、手を止めずに進捗確認や指示出しができます。
entries.summaryEn: Cursor adds Voice Chat, a live voice call with agents powered by Grok Voice. It works in the Agents Window, IDE, web and iOS, letting developers direct coding work and check progress hands-free.
entries.contentSnippet: リアルタイムの音声通話で、エージェントと会話できるようになりました。加えたい変更を声で伝えたり、エージェントが今何に取り組んでいるかを尋ねたりしながら、作業の進み具合を音声で聞くことができます。 ボイスチャットは、エージェントウィンドウ、IDE、ウェブ、そして Cursor for iOS で利用できます。 エージェントがアイドル状態でチャット入力欄が空のときに、 Start ボイスチャット というラベルの付いた波形ボタンをクリックします。このボタンは通常「送信」ボタンがある位置に表示され、音声入力用のマイクボタンの隣にあります。 iOS では、「Hey Siri, call Cursor」と話しかけて新しいエージェントとの通話を開始したり、ロック画面のライブアクティビティからミュートや通話終了を行ったりすることもできます。 音声エージェントはユーザーの話を聞いて応答し、コーディング作業をチャット内のエージェントに引き渡します。そのエージェントの実行中も、会話を続けることができます。diff で何が変更されたかを質問したり、実行の状況を確認したり、このエージェントとの過去のメッセージや通話を検索したり、ワーカーがある Project ではワーカーを切り替えたりできます。 コーディングエージェント自身も音声で伝えます。作業中は短い進捗メモを、完了時には簡潔な回答を共有するため、通常はテキストの回答全文ではなく、短い更新情報を聞くことになります。 ボイスチャットは Grok Voice で実行されます。音声は Voice 設定から、Ara、Eve、Leo、Rex、Sal をはじめとする多数の中から選べます。Privacy Mode をオンにすると、ボイスチャットはデータ保持なしで実行されます。 ボイスチャットは、以前のリリースで Voice Mode と呼ばれていた音声入力とは別の機能です。音声入力では引き続き、話した内容がテキストとしてチャット入力欄に入力され、IDE では Cmd+Shift+Space でオン/オフを切り替えられます。

It converts developer intent into a Verus specification, proves AI-generated code meets it for every input, and uses tests where proofs aren't practical. Developers review intent, not every line. entries.contentSnippet: エージェントの登場でコードを書くコストは下がりましたが、ユーザーが作るアプリやツールのほとんどは、いまだに localhost の外に出ることがありません。 これからは、Cursor 上でライブアプリを直接構築し、リンクで共有できます。作りたいものを説明するだけで、アプリの構築からデータベースのセットアップ、認証の設定、デプロイまで、あとはすべて Cursor が引き受けます。 今回のリリースにより、組織内の誰もが自分の業務に役立つツールを構築し、チームメンバーと共有できるようになりました。Cursor を更新して、ぜひお試しください。 はじめるには、 クラウドエージェント を起動し、アプリを構築したいと明示的に伝えます。 Cursor はウェブアプリの雛形を作成し、必要に応じて Postgres データベースを立ち上げ、Cursor SSO による認証を設定し、ホスティング環境を用意します。データウェアハウスなど、既存のシステムにアプリを接続する必要がある場合は、Cursor が必要なシークレットの入力を求めます。 アプリを公開する際は、一意のドメインを選ぶだけで、Cursor がすぐにアクセスできる公開リンクを発行します。 Cursor 社内では、営業、オペレーション、法務、財務、エンジニアリングなど、さまざまな部門のユーザーが社内アプリを構築しています。特に役に立っているものの例は次のとおりです。 Cursor は、Cursor Origin と GitHub 上の新規または既存のリポジトリからアプリをデプロイできます。GitLab など他の Git プロバイダーのサポートも近日公開予定です。 アプリを公開する際、Cursor は決定論的なチェックとエージェント型のセキュリティチェックを実行し、アプリのファイルに書き込まれたシークレットや露出した認証情報など、よくある Issue を検出します。チェックに失敗した場合は、何を修正すべきかをエージェントが知らせます。チェックに合格し、明示的に公開操作を行うまで、アプリが公開されることはありません。

entries.summaryEn: VS Code 1.145 lets remote agent sessions preview apps and use interactive canvases, adds cron-based automation schedules, and reduces chat noise. The Local harness is deprecated, so users should plan their move to the Copilot harness before February 2027.
entries.contentSnippet: 🎬 Watch the VS Code session recordings from Microsoft Ignite. ⚠️ The Local harness is deprecated and will be removed in February 2027. Learn about the move to the Copilot harness. Update 1.145.1 : The update addresses these issues . Update 1.145.2 : The update addresses these issues . Update 1.145.3 : The update addresses these security issues . .deb .rpm .tar.gz Arm instructions Snap This week, your remote agent sessions feel a bit more local. Preview apps and use canvases right in VS Code, fine-tune automation schedules with cron, and turn down the noise in chat. And when you need a break, Blobby is ready to play. Remote agents : Preview apps and use interactive canvases from remote agent sessions without leaving the Agents window. Automations : Run recurring agent tasks on custom schedules beyond the built-in presets with cron.
